+# Pantoken A2UI catalog for agent-generated UI
+
+## Goal
+
+Publish a versioned A2UI catalog that gives agents a constrained Pantoken component vocabulary,
+using Pantoken's existing web-component rendering, property mapping, icon handling, and interaction
+behavior where those contracts exist. Keep the canonical catalog and agent-facing material in
+`ai/`. Do not create native Pantoken UI kits or duplicate component implementations as part of this
+work.
+
+## Current state
+
+- Work is on the existing `a2ui` branch. Its two existing commits add the A2UI skill and shared agent
+  guidance; catalog implementation has not started.
+- Flutter, Swift, and Compose currently emit design-token constants, not Pantoken component
+  renderers. There is no native UI implementation to adapt.
+- `formats/components` records are CSS-oriented. Their ability to describe A2UI's typed properties,
+  child slots, and events is not established.
+- The official A2UI guidance currently documents Universal Web Components and Basic Catalog
+  composition. Compatibility still needs verification against the exact released SDK versions
+  selected for Pantoken; do not treat documentation for floating versions as the shipping contract.
+
+## Proposed scope and decisions to confirm
+
+- **Web-first v1:** support React, Lit, and Angular through one A2UI Universal Web Component bridge
+  over `@pantoken/web-components`, provided the version gate confirms the selected SDK contracts.
+- **Native clients:** no Flutter, SwiftUI, or Jetpack Compose registration adapters or UI kits in
+  this project. Mark them as schema-only/no Pantoken component renderer in the support matrix.
+  Native apps continue using A2UI's Basic Catalog and Pantoken's existing native token outputs; do
+  not advertise the Pantoken custom catalog as registered on those clients.
+- **Catalog and package boundaries:** canonical catalog, generator, and agent guidance live in
+  `ai/`; the thin browser bridge lives with the existing web components. Do not make a blanket
+  package that re-exports every renderer.
+- **Coverage claim:** first spike Button, Tabs, and Tooltip. After the spike, define the v1 set as
+  the A2UI-usable web components for which the source contract can accurately specify properties,
+  children, icons, and events. Do not promise every CSS record or claim complete coverage until a
+  coverage audit demonstrates it. Utilities and declarations are not catalog components unless a
+  real renderer exposes them as components.
+- **Basic Catalog:** preserve its standard layout vocabulary and compose Pantoken-specific
+  components with it where supported.
+- **Docs:** add a searchable, browse-only catalog with schemas, support status, and raw JSON.
+  Registration examples are web-only; native has no registration snippets. Defer live previews.
+
+## Architecture and safety constraints
+
+- Verify, before implementation, the released React/Lit/Angular A2UI SDK versions and their
+  Universal Web Component registration contract, supported protocol versions, and whether/how a
+  custom catalog composes with the Basic Catalog. Record the evidence and exact versions. If any
+  required contract is unavailable or incompatible, stop and revise the bridge design rather than
+  infer it.
+- The schema spike must identify the canonical source for typed properties, child/slot rules,
+  events/functions, icons, and accessibility behavior. Do not assume CSS modifier metadata supplies
+  these contracts. If substantial new metadata or renderer behavior is required, revise the coverage
+  and release scope before building the catalog.
+- Before bridge implementation, define a strict component and property allowlist; reject unknown
+  components and props, raw HTML/markup, unsafe URLs, unrecognized icon names, and arbitrary action
+  or function execution. Map allowed actions only to explicit Pantoken behavior and safe events.
+  Add negative tests for rejected inputs.
+- Keep the runtime bridge browser-safe and Node-free. Do not import `@cssdoc/*`, catalog generators,
+  or other build-only code into `renderers/web-components`; generation belongs in `ai/` build
+  tooling.
+- Give the catalog a stable, immutable, versioned `catalogId` (a `/vN/` identity, not a mutable
+  `latest` URL). Treat component/prop removal, renames, required-prop changes, and incompatible
+  semantics as breaking; additions that preserve old messages are additive. Tie regeneration and
+  explicit version changes to the InstUI upgrade/deprecation workflow so upstream drift cannot
+  silently alter the published contract.
+- Update `ASSURANCE.md` and `SECURITY.md` if the catalog or bridge adds input surfaces or controls.
+
+## Milestones
+
+1. **Verification and schema/security spike.** Pin the relevant A2UI SDK versions and document
+   protocol, universal registration, and Basic Catalog findings. Inspect Button, Tabs, and Tooltip
+   across component records and web renderers; produce an initial coverage matrix and identify
+   missing canonical metadata. Specify the allowlist and negative security cases. This milestone is
+   a gate: revise or stop if the evidence does not support the proposed web bridge or scope.
+2. **Catalog contract and generator.** Add the canonical, versioned web catalog in `ai/`, generate
+   it from validated source metadata, and test schema validity, stable IDs, coverage, and drift.
+   Publish the catalog and appropriate agent guidance with a changeset for changed package output.
+3. **Universal web bridge.** Implement the thin A2UI Universal Web Component integration over
+   existing web components. Reuse existing property conversion, icon resolution, and behaviors;
+   add no native UI kit and no duplicated rendering implementation. Test allowlisted props, nested
+   children, events, icons, and rejected input.
+4. **Docs catalog browser.** Generate static browser data from the same catalog source. Reuse the
+   shadcn browser's search/static-data patterns, not its install commands or previews. Show
+   per-client support, schemas, props, children, actions, raw JSON, and web-only registration
+   examples; localize new UI in English and Hungarian.
+5. **Agent evaluations, release, and drift gates.** Keep existing A2UI token-theming evaluations.
+   Add positive web catalog routing and negative evaluations for invented components, invalid
+   properties, and unsupported native registration. Update `use-a2ui` so agents use the Pantoken
+   catalog for supported web clients and the Basic Catalog plus Pantoken tokens for native. Run
+   focused tests, security checks, package checks, and publish checks. Ship each independently
+   releasable package change with its changeset; follow repository release policy for docs-only
+   work.
+
+## Expected source areas
+
+- `formats/components/src/` and `renderers/web-components/src/` — source-contract audit and web
+  component behavior.
+- `ai/pantoken-ai/catalogs/`, `ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/`, and package metadata — canonical catalog,
+  generation, published assets, and version/drift checks.
+- `renderers/web-components/` — thin Universal Web Component bridge, with no build-only imports.
+- `docs/scripts/`, `docs/a2ui/`, and `docs/.vitepress/theme/` — generated static data, browser,
+  routing, localization, and focused tests.
+- `packages/scaffold/skills/use-a2ui/` and `packages/scaffold/assets/` — updated skill and shared
+  consumer guidance.
+- `ai/pantoken-ai/evals/` and renderer tests — positive and negative agent/bridge behavior.
+- `ASSURANCE.md`, `SECURITY.md`, package documentation, and `.changeset/` — security and release
+  updates when applicable.
+
+## Verification
+
+- Record version-specific evidence for the selected A2UI SDKs, Universal Web Component support,
+  protocol compatibility, and Basic Catalog composition before implementation.
+- Use the Button/Tabs/Tooltip spike to validate schema-source sufficiency; gate any broader coverage
+  claim on the resulting audit.
+- Validate the generated catalog against the selected A2UI schema and assert its versioned ID,
+  allowlist, and drift behavior.
+- Test web registration and property/child/icon/event behavior, including unsafe/unknown inputs;
+  verify the browser runtime graph remains Node-free.
+- Verify the docs browser uses generated catalog data, localizes its UI, and labels native support
+  as schema-only without native registration examples.
+- Run existing and new A2UI Waza evaluations, focused package tests, `vp check`, and applicable
+  publish checks. Add changesets for package output and public behavior changes.

import { buttonCss } from "@pantoken/components";
import type { ElementDefinition } from "../lib/context.ts";

/**
 * `<instui-button>` — a token-styled `<button>`. The `variant` attribute maps to the `-color-<variant>`
 * modifier (`secondary`, `tertiary`, `success`, `danger`, `ai`, …); `margin` adds spacing around the
 * host (InstUI keywords like `small` / `medium large`); slotted content is the label.
 *
 * It is also a native invoker: `popovertarget` (with optional `popovertargetaction`) toggles any
 * light-DOM `[popover]` such as `<instui-context-view>`, `<instui-popover>`, or `<instui-tray>`, and
 * `command`/`commandfor` drives the command-based components (`<instui-modal>` with `--show`/`--close`,
 * etc.). The id is forwarded to the inner button via the invoker IDL, so it resolves across the shadow
 * boundary and may point forward to an element declared later in the document.
 *
 * @example
 * ```html
 * <instui-button variant="primary" margin="small">Save changes</instui-button>
 * <instui-button variant="danger" margin="small">Delete</instui-button>
 * <instui-button popovertarget="cv">Details</instui-button>
 * <instui-context-view id="cv">More about this item.</instui-context-view>
 * ```
 */
export const button: ElementDefinition = {
  name: "button",
  define: (ctx) =>
    ctx.wrapper(
      "instui-button",
      buttonCss(ctx.I),
      (host) =>
        `<button class="${ctx.variantClass("button", host)}" part="button"><slot></slot></button>`,
      { invoker: true },
    ),
};

 /**
  * `<instui-button>` — a token-styled `<button>`. The `variant` attribute maps to the `-color-<variant>`
  * modifier (`secondary`, `tertiary`, `success`, `danger`, `ai`, …); `margin` adds spacing around the
  * host (InstUI keywords like `small` / `medium large`); slotted content is the label.
  *
  * It is also a native invoker: `popovertarget` (with optional `popovertargetaction`) toggles any
  * light-DOM `[popover]` such as `<instui-context-view>`, `<instui-popover>`, or `<instui-tray>`, and
  * `command`/`commandfor` drives the command-based components (`<instui-modal>` with `--show`/`--close`,
  * etc.). The id is forwarded to the inner button via the invoker IDL, so it resolves across the shadow
  * boundary and may point forward to an element declared later in the document.
  *
  * @example
  * ```html
  * <instui-button variant="primary" margin="small">Save changes</instui-button>
  * <instui-button variant="danger" margin="small">Delete</instui-button>
  * <instui-button popovertarget="cv">Details</instui-button>
  * <instui-context-view id="cv">More about this item.</instui-context-view>
  * ```
  */

   name: "button",
   define: (ctx) =>
     ctx.wrapper(

---
name: use-a2ui
description: Inspect an app's installed A2UI renderer and apply pantoken tokens or icons through its supported theme API. Use for A2UI renderer theming or native token output, not transport-only or generic pantoken tasks.
---

# Use pantoken with A2UI

Use this skill when a consumer app combines pantoken with an A2UI renderer. Pantoken supplies
design tokens and icons; A2UI supplies the UI protocol and framework-specific renderers. For
token-only work, reuse the installed A2UI renderer rather than adding a runtime, transport, renderer,
or custom catalog.

## Do not use this skill for

Don't use this skill for A2UI protocol or transport questions that don't involve pantoken, or
generic pantoken styling without A2UI. Use it for custom catalogs only when the user explicitly
requests one.

## 1. Identify the client and versions

Inspect the app's package manifest, lockfile, and installed packages. Identify the actual A2UI
renderer, its protocol version, and how the host framework applies themes. Check the current
[official SDK table](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/) and
[client integration guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/) rather than assuming all
frameworks support the same protocol version or styling API. A2UI v1.0 delegates branding to the
renderer; don't put theme properties in v1.0 protocol messages.

## 2. Apply pantoken to the existing renderer

- **Web Basic Catalog:** Follow the current A2UI docs for its `--a2ui-*` custom properties. Read
  the installed renderer's stylesheet or version-matched docs to confirm each property. Use
  pantoken's `--instui-*` custom properties only after resolving a semantically matching,
  correctly typed token from `@pantoken/tokens`. Load `@pantoken/css` so those tokens are defined.
  Keep the mapping scoped when the app needs multiple themes; don't hard-code color values or
  invent A2UI or InstUI property names.
- **Native clients:** Use pantoken's existing target output for the host: `pantoken generate
  flutter`, `compose`, or `swift`, as appropriate. Follow the A2UI renderer's native theme API;
  CSS custom properties do not apply to native views.
- **Other web frameworks:** Choose the matching official A2UI renderer first, then use its supported
  theming mechanism. Don't assume React-specific setup applies to Lit or Angular.
- **Icons:** For surrounding web UI, use `@pantoken/web-components` or `@pantoken/icons`. For icons
  inside an A2UI surface, verify the selected catalog's icon API; only add a custom component when
  the user asks for one.

## 3. Extend only when requested

If the user asks for a custom A2UI catalog, follow A2UI's
[catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/) and the host renderer's registration
API. A catalog defines agent-facing components and functions; pantoken tokens don't implement those
components or behaviors. Preserve the renderer's accessibility, focus, and interaction contracts.
Handle protocol transports only when explicitly in scope.

## 4. Verify

Run the host app's relevant type checks and tests. Verify the theme in each supported color scheme,
including contrast and keyboard/focus behavior. Confirm every `--instui-*` reference exists in the
installed token package and every `--a2ui-*` property matches the installed A2UI renderer version.

## References

- [A2UI v1.0 protocol](https://a2ui.org/specification/v1.0-a2ui/)
- [A2UI SDKs](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/)
- [A2UI client integration](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/)
- [A2UI catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/)

Contents of https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/:
# SDKs

Official A2UI SDKs are organized into three layers:

*   **Core SDK** for shared protocol models and surface state.
*   **Agent SDK** for catalog-driven prompt generation and model output compilation.
*   **Renderer SDK** for mounting surface state in a client UI framework.

Both the Agent SDK and the Renderer SDK build on their language’s Core SDK, so server-side validation and client-side message resolution share one implementation per language. Client-server applications typically pair two layers on each side of a network boundary, such as a Python agent server communicating with a SwiftUI or Jetpack Compose client. Codebases that handle both model inference and UI rendering in the same language, such as TypeScript web apps or Dart and Flutter apps, can use all three layers together in one project.

## Core SDK

Every Agent SDK and Renderer SDK depends on its language’s Core SDK, which implements the protocol data structures, reactive state containers, and expression evaluators common to agents and clients.

### Primary functions

1.  Parses and serializes A2UI [wire messages](/concepts/messages/) across supported protocol versions (v1.0, v0.9.1, and v0.8 in TypeScript and Python).
2.  Loads [Catalog](/concepts/catalogs/) JSON Schemas and validates component hierarchies, placement constraints, and message payloads.
3.  Maintains per-surface component graphs and JSON [data model](/concepts/data-binding/) state while applying incremental updates by component ID and JSON Pointer path.
4.  Evaluates data bindings, collection templates, string interpolation expressions, function invocations, and validation checks.

### Packages

| Language   | Published packages                                                                                                                                           | Versions           | Source                                                                                               |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TypeScript | [@a2ui/web\_core](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@a2ui/web_core)                                                                                              | v0.8, v0.9.1, v1.0 | [typescript/core/web\_core](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/typescript/core/web_core) |
| Python     | [a2ui-core](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-core/)                                                                                                             | v0.8, v0.9.1, v1.0 | [python/a2ui\_core](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/python/a2ui_core)                 |
| Dart       | [a2ui\_core](https://pub.dev/packages/a2ui_core)                                                                                                             | v0.9.1, v1.0       | [dart/a2ui\_core](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/dart/a2ui_core)                     |
| Swift      | [A2UISwiftCore](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/Package.swift)   [BasicCatalog](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/Package.swift) | v0.9.1, v1.0       | [swift/core](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/swift/core)                              |
| Kotlin     | [androidx.a2ui](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/a2ui)                                                                                | v0.9.1             | [AndroidX a2ui](https://cs.android.com/androidx/platform/frameworks/support/+/androidx-main:a2ui/)   |

All v0.9.1 packages accept v0.9 wire envelopes and catalog IDs. Swift packages are distributed through Swift Package Manager from [`a2ui-project/a2ui`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui) (the `A2UISwiftCore` product exposes the `A2UICore` module), and the AndroidX group on Google Maven publishes the `a2ui-model` and `a2ui-engine` artifacts.

Most applications install a Core SDK automatically through an [Agent SDK](#agent-sdk) or [Renderer SDK](#renderer-sdk), though you can depend on a Core SDK directly to build headless state processors or custom UI adapters. To implement a Core SDK in another language, read [`blueprints/modules`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/blueprints/modules) and validate against the YAML suites in [`conformance/core`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/conformance/core).

## Agent SDK

An Agent SDK connects a language model or agent runtime to the A2UI protocol while leaving model selection, tool execution, and conversation state under your application’s control.

### Primary functions

1.  Negotiates active [Catalog](/concepts/catalogs/) definitions and protocol versions (v0.9.1 and v1.0) against the capabilities reported by the client renderer (see [Overview](/concepts/overview/)).
2.  Generates skills, system prompt instructions, and examples directly from catalog schemas and prompt instructions, replacing hand-written prompts that become outdated when components change.
3.  Compiles streaming or batch model output from [inference formats](/concepts/inference-formats/) (such as compact Express syntax, which cuts output tokens without client changes, or chunk-healed Direct JSON) into standard A2UI [wire messages](/concepts/messages/).
4.  Validates outgoing messages statefully against active surface state on the server so broken component IDs, placement violations, or schema mismatches can be fed back to the model for self-correction before transmission.
5.  Supports optional server-side [`@macro`](/guides/macros/) expansion in Python and integrates with agent frameworks and transports including [Google ADK](https://github.com/google/adk-python) and the [A2A protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org/).

### Packages

| Language   | Published packages                                                                                                                                                       | Versions           | Source                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TypeScript | [@a2ui/agent](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@a2ui/agent)                                                                                                                 | v0.9.1, v1.0       | [typescript/agents/a2ui\_agent](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/typescript/agents/a2ui_agent)                                                                                                                                                     |
| Python     | [a2ui-agent-sdk](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-agent-sdk/)   [a2ui-adk](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-adk/) (ADK)   [a2ui-a2a](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-a2a/) (A2A) | v0.8, v0.9.1, v1.0 | [python/a2ui\_agent](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/python/a2ui_agent)   [python/a2ui\_adk](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/python/a2ui_adk)   [python/a2ui\_a2a](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/python/a2ui_a2a) |
| Dart       | [a2ui\_agent](https://pub.dev/packages/a2ui_agent)                                                                                                                       | v0.9.1, v1.0       | [dart/a2ui\_agent](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/dart/a2ui_agent)                                                                                                                                                                               |

Swift and Kotlin target client-side rendering; for legacy v0.8 and v0.9 JVM servers, [`kotlin/agent_sdk_legacy`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/kotlin/agent_sdk_legacy) remains in the repository.

### Go and community SDKs

For **Go** services and CLI clients, community-maintained libraries cover server-side validation, streaming parsers, and terminal rendering—including [`satorunooshie/a2ui-go`](https://github.com/satorunooshie/a2ui-go), [`tmc/a2ui`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/tmc/a2ui), [`charmbracelet/a2tea`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/a2tea), and [`muncus/a2term`](https://github.com/muncus/a2term) (listed with version details in [Community Projects](/ecosystem/renderers/)).

To implement a conformance-verified Core or Agent SDK in Go, Rust, C#, or another language, follow the language-agnostic specifications in [`blueprints/modules`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/blueprints/modules), verify behavioral parity against the YAML suites in [`conformance/core`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/conformance/core) and [`conformance/agent`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/conformance/agent), and open a pull request to add your package to [Community Projects](/ecosystem/renderers/#how-to-submit-a-project).

See [Using a catalog in an agent](/concepts/catalogs/#using-a-catalog-in-an-agent) and [Inference Formats](/concepts/inference-formats/#how-inference-formats-stay-swappable) for TypeScript, Python, and Dart examples of configuring `A2uiGenerator`, negotiating capabilities, and compiling model responses, or run a working agent in the [Quickstart](/quickstart/).

## Renderer SDK

A Renderer SDK connects a Core SDK’s resolved surface state to a client UI framework. Official Renderer SDKs include a built-in implementation of the [Basic Catalog](/concepts/catalogs/#the-basic-catalog) styled through the host framework’s theming system, and let you register custom catalogs with per-component rendering logic and local functions (see [How to Define a Catalog](/guides/defining-a-catalog/)).

### Primary functions

1.  Applies incremental [surface, component, and data model updates](/concepts/messages/) across supported protocol versions (v0.9.1, v1.0, and v0.8 on Web), updating only changed subtrees so unchanged siblings keep focus and local UI state.
2.  Evaluates [reactive data bindings](/concepts/data-binding/), nested collection scopes, relative JSON Pointers, and local two-way input edits.
3.  Executes [local catalog functions](/concepts/catalogs/#functions) and [reactive validation checks](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#component-validation--check-rules), enforcing v1.0 caller and user-activation rules.
4.  Builds capability and data-model sync metadata payloads for your transport layer, dispatches user action events and structured error messages, and handles v1.0 bidirectional function RPCs.
5.  Maps protocol accessibility attributes to host accessibility APIs across Flutter, Web WAI-ARIA, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose.

### Packages

| Framework       | Published packages                                                                                                                                                                          | Versions           | Source                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Malicious agents could attempt to spoof legitimate interfaces to deceive users (phishing), inject malicious scripts via property values (XSS), or generate excessive layout complexity to degrade client performance (DoS). If your application supports optional embedded content (such as iframes or web views), additional care must be taken to prevent exposure to malicious external sites. data.reasoningText:
**Making an important decision**

I’m facing an important decision and need to ask the user for their input. I have some findings to share: the latest versions are React/Lit/web_core .15.0 and Angular .14.0. The npm package sources for React and Angular use web_core/v0_9/universal, which raises caution for supporting v1, despite the official SDK stating all support v1.0. 

I recommend staging common protocol v0.9.1 and starting with a small pilot like Button + Tooltip, while noting the user’s desire for broader scope coverage.

**Clarifying metadata recommendations**

I’m considering the review's suggestion to start with “spike 2 or 3 components first” like Button, Tabs, and Tooltip to check the metadata. This aligns with the recommendation for a limited pilot. I need to note that the official A2UI docs still claim v1.0 support, but the current React/Angular Universal bundles import v0_9, so I won't advertise v1.0 until that's confirmed. For v0.9.1, it's essential to verify that each surface binds to a single `catalogId`. Let's opt for shared universal registration v0.9.1, even though `catalog.json` may lack `protocolVersion`.

**Deciding on protocol options**

I’m evaluating the protocol recommendations. The first option suggests using v0.9.1 for the initial web catalog, which combines Basic and Pantoken into one merged catalog, making it a straightforward SDK path but sacrifices something of the older protocol. Another option proposes keeping v1.0 as the target but deferring implementation until v1 Universal is verified, which keeps things modern but delays progress. Finally, I could support both by shipping v0.9.1 Universal now and developing a separate v1.0 track when it's compatible, though that would require more work.

result.content:
# Pantoken A2UI catalog for agent-generated UI

## Goal

Publish a versioned A2UI catalog that gives agents a constrained Pantoken component vocabulary,
using Pantoken's existing web-component rendering, property mapping, icon handling, and interaction
behavior where those contracts exist. Keep the canonical catalog and agent-facing material in
`ai/`. Do not create native Pantoken UI kits or duplicate component implementations as part of this
work.

## Current state

- Work is on the existing `a2ui` branch. Its two existing commits add the A2UI skill and shared agent
  guidance; catalog implementation has not started.
- Flutter, Swift, and Compose currently emit design-token constants, not Pantoken component
  renderers. There is no native UI implementation to adapt.
- `formats/components` records are CSS-oriented. Their ability to describe A2UI's typed properties,
  child slots, and events is not established.
- The A2UI Universal Web Components guide documents a Zod `ComponentApi` plus
  `A2uiLitElement`/`WebComponentImplementation`, and says the host renderers register these
  implementations. The latest published packages checked are `@a2ui/web_core` 0.15.0,
  `@a2ui/react` 0.15.0, `@a2ui/lit` 0.15.0, and `@a2ui/angular` 0.14.0.
- The published React 0.15.0 and Angular 0.14.0 renderer bundles use
  `@a2ui/web_core/v0_9/universal`; Lit 0.15.0 exposes the universal element API and a v0.9 entry.
  The SDK overview lists v1.0 support for these frameworks, but the shipped Universal Component
  path for React and Angular is versioned to v0.9. This does not yet establish a common v1.0
  Universal Component contract across all three.
- A2UI v1.0 documentation shows Basic Catalog components being reused in a custom `Catalog` and
  allows a component to identify a second catalog with `@catalogId`. The v0.9.1 guide says a
  surface binds to a single `catalogId`, so the web client must register a combined Basic +
  Pantoken catalog; its exact catalog/agent composition API remains to be pinned.
- The schema spike confirms that the CSS component records do not define typed A2UI properties,
  child slots, or actions. Button's web-element contract is only described in JSDoc; Tabs requires
  a coordinated tablist/tab/panel structure and keyboard behavior; Tooltip has `tip`, `placement`,
  delays, and slotted trigger content, with text content rendered safely via `textContent`.
  Therefore full catalog coverage is not established by existing metadata. The coverage audit
  must decide which components can be supported without inventing undocumented behavior.

## Confirmed scope and decisions

- **Web-first v1:** support React, Lit, and Angular through one A2UI Universal Web Component bridge
  over `@pantoken/web-components`, provided the version gate confirms the selected SDK contracts.
  The user confirmed this boundary.
- **Native clients:** no Flutter, SwiftUI, or Jetpack Compose registration adapters or UI kits in
  this project. Mark them as schema-only/no Pantoken component renderer in the support matrix.
  Native apps continue using A2UI's Basic Catalog and Pantoken's existing native token outputs; do
  not advertise the Pantoken custom catalog as registered on those clients.
- **Catalog and package boundaries:** canonical catalog, generator, and agent guidance live in
  `ai/`; the thin browser bridge lives with the existing web components. Do not make a blanket
  package that re-exports every renderer.
- **Coverage claim:** first spike Button, Tabs, and Tooltip. After the spike, define the v1 set as
  the A2UI-usable web components for which the source contract can accurately specify properties,
  children, icons, and events. Do not promise every CSS record or claim complete coverage until a
  coverage audit demonstrates it. Utilities and declarations are not catalog components unless a
  real renderer exposes them as components.
- **Basic Catalog:** preserve its standard layout vocabulary and compose Pantoken-specific
  components with it where supported.
- **Protocol remains a gate decision:** either target the currently evident common Universal
  Component path (v0.9.1, with a merged Basic + Pantoken catalog), or keep v1.0 and wait for or add
  compatible framework-specific registration. Do not silently mix the v1.0 catalog contract with
  renderers whose released Universal path is v0.9.
- **Docs:** add a searchable, browse-only catalog with schemas, support status, and raw JSON.
  Registration examples are web-only; native has no registration snippets. Defer live previews.

## Architecture and safety constraints

- Verify, before implementation, the released React/Lit/Angular A2UI SDK versions and their
  Universal Web Component registration contract, supported protocol versions, and whether/how a
  custom catalog composes with the Basic Catalog. Record the evidence and exact versions. If any
  required contract is unavailable or incompatible, stop and revise the bridge design rather than
  infer it.
- The schema spike must identify the canonical source for typed properties, child/slot rules,
  events/functions, icons, and accessibility behavior. Do not assume CSS modifier metadata supplies
  these contracts. If substantial new metadata or renderer behavior is required, revise the coverage
  and release scope before building the catalog.
- Before bridge implementation, define a strict component and property allowlist; reject unknown
  components and props, raw HTML/markup, unsafe URLs, unrecognized icon names, and arbitrary action
  or function execution. Map allowed actions only to explicit Pantoken behavior and safe events.
  Add negative tests for rejected inputs.
- Keep the runtime bridge browser-safe and Node-free. Do not import `@cssdoc/*`, catalog generators,
  or other build-only code into `renderers/web-components`; generation belongs in `ai/` build
  tooling.
- Give the catalog a stable, immutable, versioned `catalogId` (a `/vN/` identity, not a mutable
  `latest` URL). Treat component/prop removal, renames, required-prop changes, and incompatible
  semantics as breaking; additions that preserve old messages are additive. Tie regeneration and
  explicit version changes to the InstUI upgrade/deprecation workflow so upstream drift cannot
  silently alter the published contract.
- Update `ASSURANCE.md` and `SECURITY.md` if the catalog or bridge adds input surfaces or controls.

## Milestones

1. **Verification and schema/security spike.** Pin the relevant A2UI SDK versions and document
   protocol, universal registration, and Basic Catalog findings. Inspect Button, Tabs, and Tooltip
   across component records and web renderers; produce an initial coverage matrix and identify
   missing canonical metadata. Specify the allowlist and negative security cases. This milestone is
   a gate: revise or stop if the evidence does not support the proposed web bridge or scope.
2. **Catalog contract and generator.** Add the canonical, versioned web catalog in `ai/`, generate
   it from validated source metadata, and test schema validity, stable IDs, coverage, and drift.
   Publish the catalog and appropriate agent guidance with a changeset for changed package output.
3. **Universal web bridge.** Implement the thin A2UI Universal Web Component integration over
   existing web components. Reuse existing property conversion, icon resolution, and behaviors;
   add no native UI kit and no duplicated rendering implementation. Test allowlisted props, nested
   children, events, icons, and rejected input.
4. **Docs catalog browser.** Generate static browser data from the same catalog source. Reuse the
   shadcn browser's search/static-data patterns, not its install commands or previews. Show
   per-client support, schemas, props, children, actions, raw JSON, and web-only registration
   examples; localize new UI in English and Hungarian.
5. **Agent evaluations, release, and drift gates.** Keep existing A2UI token-theming evaluations.
   Add positive web catalog routing and negative evaluations for invented components, invalid
   properties, and unsupported native registration. Update `use-a2ui` so agents use the Pantoken
   catalog for supported web clients and the Basic Catalog plus Pantoken tokens for native. Run
   focused tests, security checks, package checks, and publish checks. Ship each independently
   releasable package change with its changeset; follow repository release policy for docs-only
   work.

## Expected source areas

- `formats/components/src/` and `renderers/web-components/src/` — source-contract audit and web
  component behavior.
- `ai/pantoken-ai/catalogs/`, `ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/`, and package metadata — canonical catalog,
  generation, published assets, and version/drift checks.
- `renderers/web-components/` — thin Universal Web Component bridge, with no build-only imports.
- `docs/scripts/`, `docs/a2ui/`, and `docs/.vitepress/theme/` — generated static data, browser,
  routing, localization, and focused tests.
- `packages/scaffold/skills/use-a2ui/` and `packages/scaffold/assets/` — updated skill and shared
  consumer guidance.
- `ai/pantoken-ai/evals/` and renderer tests — positive and negative agent/bridge behavior.
- `ASSURANCE.md`, `SECURITY.md`, package documentation, and `.changeset/` — security and release
  updates when applicable.

## Verification

- Record version-specific evidence for the selected A2UI SDKs, Universal Web Component support,
  protocol compatibility, and Basic Catalog composition before implementation.
- Use the Button/Tabs/Tooltip spike to validate schema-source sufficiency; gate any broader coverage
  claim on the resulting audit.
- Validate the generated catalog against the selected A2UI schema and assert its versioned ID,
  allowlist, and drift behavior.
- Test web registration and property/child/icon/event behavior, including unsafe/unknown inputs;
  verify the browser runtime graph remains Node-free.
- Verify the docs browser uses generated catalog data, localizes its UI, and labels native support
  as schema-only without native registration examples.
- Run existing and new A2UI Waza evaluations, focused package tests, `vp check`, and applicable
  publish checks. Add changesets for package output and public behavior changes.

data.requestMessages:
[{"role":"system","content":"Task: Detect whether the CURRENT MESSAGE expresses frustration with an AI coding assistant.

Two consecutive user messages from a chat with an AI assistant. The AI responded between them (you can't see that response).

- **[PREVIOUS MESSAGE]**: the user's earlier message
- **[CURRENT MESSAGE]**: the message to classify

## Decision rules

Answer **true** if the user is unhappy with what the AI did.

**True signals — user blames or is upset with AI:**
- AI output is wrong: "not what I asked", "your understanding is wrong"
- AI ignored instructions: "I told you X", "I explicitly asked", "why did you change Y"
- AI did unwanted things: "why are you adding X?", "I never asked for Z"
- AI caused regression: "stopped working after your changes", "broken now"
- Exasperation at AI: "why do you keep...", ALL CAPS displeasure
- Sarcasm/distrust: "be honest", "I take your word for it.."
- Dismissing AI: "nevermind", "this is silly"
- Rejecting AI choices: "remove X. why would Y?"
- Commands to stop AI: "stop triggering X", "DONT RUN X"
- Displeasure at AI result: "still wayy too verbose", "no expressions, no charisma"
- Comparing AI unfavorably: "Google works but yours doesn't"
- "still [problem]" when AI was supposed to fix it and user sounds annoyed
- Terse negative + challenge: "no. why would X?"

**False — reporting or instructing, NOT frustrated:**
- Bug reports: "not working", "broken", "CI failed", "same error", "didn't work"
- Negatives: "nope", "no", "no it did not"
- Instructions: "fix", "try again", "use X instead", "don't do that"
- Questions: "where is X?", "seems incomplete?"
- Follow-ups: "still don't see it", "same issue"
- Behavior descriptions: "when I click X nothing happens", "it does nothing"
- User's issues: "I messed up", "ah darn"
- Pasted logs/errors without emotional commentary

Respond with ONLY a JSON object:
{"frustration": true/false, "confidence": "high/medium/low", "evidence": "≤15 words"}"},{"role":"user","content":"[PREVIOUS MESSAGE]
The plan’s biggest problem is that the native adapters can’t “reuse existing Pantoken renderers”, because there aren’t any to reuse. Otherwise the structure holds up.

### Blocking
**1. Flutter, SwiftUI, and Compose have no component renderers.**

- `platforms/flutter`, `platforms/swift`, and `platforms/compose` each contain a single src/index.ts. They generate token constants (see the compose README: “numeric constants… reference them straight from composables”).
- Steps 3 and 5 and the “complete coverage” decision assume there’s something to wrap, and there isn’t.
- “Cover every component on every client” would mean writing and maintaining native Pantoken UI kits in Dart, Swift, and Kotlin. That’s a large new product, and it contradicts the stated “no duplicate implementations” goal.
- Decision for you: either (a) scope v1 to web, which covers React, Lit, and Angular through the web-component bridge, and ship native catalog-schema support only, or (b) make the native kits an explicit separate project.
- Recommendation: (a). On native, agents would use the Basic Catalog themed by the existing token output, which is what `use-a2ui` does today. The catalog JSON stays client-agnostic, and the coverage matrix marks native as “schema only”.

### Should fix

Task: Detect whether the CURRENT MESSAGE expresses frustration with an AI coding assistant.

Two consecutive user messages from a chat with an AI assistant. The AI responded between them (you can't see that response).

- **[PREVIOUS MESSAGE]**: the user's earlier message
- **[CURRENT MESSAGE]**: the message to classify

## Decision rules

Answer **true** if the user is unhappy with what the AI did.

**True signals — user blames or is upset with AI:**
- AI output is wrong: "not what I asked", "your understanding is wrong"
- AI ignored instructions: "I told you X", "I explicitly asked", "why did you change Y"
- AI did unwanted things: "why are you adding X?", "I never asked for Z"
- AI caused regression: "stopped working after your changes", "broken now"
- Exasperation at AI: "why do you keep...", ALL CAPS displeasure
- Sarcasm/distrust: "be honest", "I take your word for it.."
- Dismissing AI: "nevermind", "this is silly"
- Rejecting AI choices: "remove X. why would Y?"
- Commands to stop AI: "stop triggering X", "DONT RUN X"
- Displeasure at AI result: "still wayy too verbose", "no expressions, no charisma"
- Comparing AI unfavorably: "Google works but yours doesn't"
- "still [problem]" when AI was supposed to fix it and user sounds annoyed
- Terse negative + challenge: "no. why would X?"

- Bug reports: "not working", "broken", "CI failed", "same error", "didn't work"
- Negatives: "nope", "no", "no it did not"
- Instructions: "fix", "try again", "use X instead", "don't do that"

- Follow-ups: "still don't see it", "same issue"
- Behavior descriptions: "when I click X nothing happens", "it does nothing"
- User's issues: "I messed up", "ah darn"
- Pasted logs/errors without emotional commentary

{"frustration": true/false, "confidence": "high/medium/low", "evidence": "≤15 words"}

result.content:
# Pantoken A2UI catalog for agent-generated UI

## Goal

Publish a versioned A2UI catalog that gives agents a constrained Pantoken component vocabulary,
using Pantoken's existing web-component rendering, property mapping, icon handling, and interaction
behavior where those contracts exist. Keep the canonical catalog and agent-facing material in
`ai/`. Do not create native Pantoken UI kits or duplicate component implementations as part of this
work.

## Current state

- Work is on the existing `a2ui` branch. Its two existing commits add the A2UI skill and shared agent
  guidance; catalog implementation has not started.
- Flutter, Swift, and Compose currently emit design-token constants, not Pantoken component
  renderers. There is no native UI implementation to adapt.
- `formats/components` records are CSS-oriented. Their ability to describe A2UI's typed properties,
  child slots, and events is not established.
- The A2UI Universal Web Components guide documents a Zod `ComponentApi` plus
  `A2uiLitElement`/`WebComponentImplementation`, and says the host renderers register these
  implementations. The latest published packages checked are `@a2ui/web_core` 0.15.0,
  `@a2ui/react` 0.15.0, `@a2ui/lit` 0.15.0, and `@a2ui/angular` 0.14.0.
- The published React 0.15.0 and Angular 0.14.0 renderer bundles use
  `@a2ui/web_core/v0_9/universal`; Lit 0.15.0 exposes the universal element API and a v0.9 entry.
  The SDK overview lists v1.0 support for these frameworks, but the shipped Universal Component
  path for React and Angular is versioned to v0.9. This does not yet establish a common v1.0
  Universal Component contract across all three.
- A2UI v1.0 documentation shows Basic Catalog components being reused in a custom `Catalog` and
  allows a component to identify a second catalog with `@catalogId`. The v0.9.1 guide says a
  surface binds to a single `catalogId`, so the web client must register a combined Basic +
  Pantoken catalog; its exact catalog/agent composition API remains to be pinned.
- The schema spike confirms that the CSS component records do not define typed A2UI properties,
  child slots, or actions. Button's web-element contract is only described in JSDoc; Tabs requires
  a coordinated tablist/tab/panel structure and keyboard behavior; Tooltip has `tip`, `placement`,
  delays, and slotted trigger content, with text content rendered safely via `textContent`.
  Therefore full catalog coverage is not established by existing metadata. The coverage audit
  must decide which components can be supported without inventing undocumented behavior.

## Confirmed scope and decisions

- **Web-first v1:** support React, Lit, and Angular through one A2UI Universal Web Component bridge
  over `@pantoken/web-components`, using protocol v0.9.1, the common Universal path evident in the
  current published React and Angular packages. Do not claim v1.0 Universal support; add it only in
  a separate follow-up after the released framework SDK contract is verified.
- **Native clients:** no Flutter, SwiftUI, or Jetpack Compose registration adapters or UI kits in
  this project. Mark them as schema-only/no Pantoken component renderer in the support matrix.
  Native apps continue using A2UI's Basic Catalog and Pantoken's existing native token outputs; do
  not advertise the Pantoken custom catalog as registered on those clients.
- **Catalog and package boundaries:** canonical catalog, generator, and agent guidance live in
  `ai/`; the thin browser bridge lives with the existing web components. Do not make a blanket
  package that re-exports every renderer.
- **Coverage claim:** the initial catalog supports Button and Tooltip with explicit allowlisted
  schemas. Defer Tabs and other elements until each has an authored typed contract; Tabs needs a
  coordinated tablist/tab/panel schema that its CSS record does not provide. Do not promise every
  CSS record or claim complete coverage. Utilities and declarations are not catalog components
  unless a real renderer exposes them as components.
- **Basic Catalog:** preserve its standard layout vocabulary and compose Pantoken-specific
  components with it where supported.
- **Protocol/catalog interaction:** v0.9.1 binds a surface to one `catalogId`; register and supply
  a combined Basic + Pantoken catalog under that ID. Do not use v1.0's per-component `@catalogId`
  semantics in the v0.9.1 catalog.
- **Docs:** add a searchable, browse-only catalog with schemas, support status, and raw JSON.
  Registration examples are web-only; native has no registration snippets. Defer live previews.

## Architecture and safety constraints

- The version gate found a mismatch between the current SDK overview and published renderer
  bundles. Use the common released v0.9.1 Universal path now; v1.0 stays deferred until React,
  Lit, and Angular all expose a version-matched Universal Component contract.
- In v0.9.1, merge the Basic Catalog and Pantoken component implementations into one client catalog
  with one `catalogId`. Verify the exact TypeScript composition API and produce a matching
  agent-facing catalog; do not copy undocumented Basic schemas or silently mix protocol versions.
- The schema spike must identify the canonical source for typed properties, child/slot rules,
  events/functions, icons, and accessibility behavior. Do not assume CSS modifier metadata supplies
  these contracts. If substantial new metadata or renderer behavior is required, revise the coverage
  and release scope before building the catalog.
- Before bridge implementation, define a strict component and property allowlist; reject unknown
  components and props, raw HTML/markup, unsafe URLs, unrecognized icon names, and arbitrary action
  or function execution. Map allowed actions only to explicit Pantoken behavior and safe events.
  Add negative tests for rejected inputs.
- Keep the runtime bridge browser-safe and Node-free. Do not import `@cssdoc/*`, catalog generators,
  or other build-only code into `renderers/web-components`; generation belongs in `ai/` build
  tooling.
- Give the catalog a stable, immutable, versioned `catalogId` (a `/vN/` identity, not a mutable
  `latest` URL). Treat component/prop removal, renames, required-prop changes, and incompatible
  semantics as breaking; additions that preserve old messages are additive. Tie regeneration and
  explicit version changes to the InstUI upgrade/deprecation workflow so upstream drift cannot
  silently alter the published contract.
- Update `ASSURANCE.md` and `SECURITY.md` if the catalog or bridge adds input surfaces or controls.

## Milestones

1. **Verification and schema/security spike.** Record the exact published package versions and the
   protocol mismatch. Inspect Button, Tabs, and Tooltip; establish the limited initial coverage and
   missing canonical metadata. Specify the allowlist and negative security cases before
   implementation. This gate is complete; it does not establish v1.0 Universal support.
2. **Catalog contract and generator.** Add the canonical v0.9.1 web catalog in `ai/` for Button
   and Tooltip, with explicit typed properties/actions/children, a stable versioned `catalogId`,
   and the matching Basic Catalog composition. Test schema validity, coverage, and drift. Publish
   the catalog and agent guidance with changesets for changed package output.
3. **Universal web bridge.** Implement the thin v0.9.1 A2UI Universal Web Component integration
   over existing Button and Tooltip elements. Reuse existing property conversion and behavior; add
   no native UI kit and no duplicated rendering implementation. Test allowlisted props, children,
   actions, and rejected input.
4. **Docs catalog browser.** Generate static browser data from the same catalog source. Reuse the
   shadcn browser's search/static-data patterns, not its install commands or previews. Show
   per-client support, schemas, props, children, actions, raw JSON, and v0.9.1 web-only registration
   examples; localize new UI in English and Hungarian. Label Tabs and other unshipped components
   unsupported rather than implying full coverage.
5. **Agent evaluations, release, and drift gates.** Keep existing A2UI token-theming evaluations.
   Add positive web catalog routing and negative evaluations for invented components, invalid
   properties, and unsupported native registration. Update `use-a2ui` so agents use the Pantoken
   catalog for supported web clients and the Basic Catalog plus Pantoken tokens for native. Run
   focused tests, security checks, package checks, and publish checks. Ship each independently
   releasable package change with its changeset; follow repository release policy for docs-only
   work.

## Expected source areas

- `formats/components/src/` and `renderers/web-components/src/` — source-contract audit and web
  component behavior.
- `ai/pantoken-ai/catalogs/`, `ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/`, and package metadata — canonical catalog,
  generation, published assets, and version/drift checks.
- `renderers/web-components/` — thin Universal Web Component bridge, with no build-only imports.
- `docs/scripts/`, `docs/a2ui/`, and `docs/.vitepress/theme/` — generated static data, browser,
  routing, localization, and focused tests.
- `packages/scaffold/skills/use-a2ui/` and `packages/scaffold/assets/` — updated skill and shared
  consumer guidance.
- `ai/pantoken-ai/evals/` and renderer tests — positive and negative agent/bridge behavior.
- `ASSURANCE.md`, `SECURITY.md`, package documentation, and `.changeset/` — security and release
  updates when applicable.

## Verification

- Validate the v0.9.1 Universal bridge against the exact released SDK versions and confirm one
  combined Basic + Pantoken catalog works in each web client.
- Use the Button/Tabs/Tooltip spike to validate schema-source sufficiency; test only Button and
  Tooltip in the initial catalog, and mark Tabs/other components unsupported until their contracts
  are defined.
- Validate the generated catalog against the selected A2UI schema and assert its versioned ID,
  allowlist, and drift behavior.
- Test web registration and property/child/icon/event behavior, including unsafe/unknown inputs;
  verify the browser runtime graph remains Node-free.
- Verify the docs browser uses generated catalog data, localizes its UI, and labels native support
  as schema-only without native registration examples.
- Run existing and new A2UI Waza evaluations, focused package tests, `vp check`, and applicable
  publish checks. Add changesets for package output and public behavior changes.

# Pantoken A2UI catalog for agent-generated UI

## Goal

Publish a versioned A2UI catalog that gives agents a constrained Pantoken component vocabulary,
using Pantoken's existing web-component rendering, property mapping, icon handling, and interaction
behavior where those contracts exist. Keep the canonical catalog and agent-facing material in
`ai/`. Do not create native Pantoken UI kits or duplicate component implementations as part of this
work.

## Current state

- Work is on the existing `a2ui` branch. Its two existing commits add the A2UI skill and shared agent
  guidance; catalog implementation has not started.
- Flutter, Swift, and Compose currently emit design-token constants, not Pantoken component
  renderers. There is no native UI implementation to adapt.
- `formats/components` records are CSS-oriented. Their ability to describe A2UI's typed properties,
  child slots, and events is not established.
- The A2UI Universal Web Components guide documents a Zod `ComponentApi` plus
  `A2uiLitElement`/`WebComponentImplementation`, and says the host renderers register these
  implementations. The latest published packages checked are `@a2ui/web_core` 0.15.0,
  `@a2ui/react` 0.15.0, `@a2ui/lit` 0.15.0, and `@a2ui/angular` 0.14.0.
- The published React 0.15.0 and Angular 0.14.0 renderer bundles use
  `@a2ui/web_core/v0_9/universal`; Lit 0.15.0 exposes the universal element API and a v0.9 entry.
  The SDK overview lists v1.0 support for these frameworks, but the shipped Universal Component
  path for React and Angular is versioned to v0.9. This does not yet establish a common v1.0
  Universal Component contract across all three; do not infer v1.0 compatibility from the overview
  alone.
- A2UI v1.0 documentation shows Basic Catalog components being reused in a custom `Catalog` and
  allows a component to identify a second catalog with `@catalogId`. The v0.9.1 guide says a
  surface binds to a single `catalogId`, so the web client must register a combined Basic +
  Pantoken catalog; its exact catalog/agent composition API remains to be pinned.
- The schema spike confirms that the CSS component records do not define typed A2UI properties,
  child slots, or actions. Button's web-element contract is only described in JSDoc; Tabs requires
  a coordinated tablist/tab/panel structure and keyboard behavior; Tooltip has `tip`, `placement`,
  delays, and slotted trigger content, with text content rendered safely via `textContent`.
  Therefore full catalog coverage is not established by existing metadata. The coverage audit
  must decide which components can be supported without inventing undocumented behavior.

## Confirmed scope and decisions

- **Protocol:** use A2UI 1.0 only, as directed. Do not downgrade to 0.9.
- **Web-first v1:** target React, Lit, and Angular through one A2UI Universal Web Component bridge
  over `@pantoken/web-components` only after exact released SDK versions prove v1.0 support. The
  latest React/Angular packages checked do not yet establish that contract.
- **Native clients:** no Flutter, SwiftUI, or Jetpack Compose registration adapters or UI kits in
  this project. Mark them as schema-only/no Pantoken component renderer in the support matrix.
  Native apps continue using A2UI's Basic Catalog and Pantoken's existing native token outputs; do
  not advertise the Pantoken custom catalog as registered on those clients.
- **Catalog and package boundaries:** canonical catalog, generator, and agent guidance live in
  `ai/`; the thin browser bridge lives with the existing web components. Do not make a blanket
  package that re-exports every renderer.
- **Coverage claim:** the initial catalog supports Button and Tooltip with explicit allowlisted
  schemas. Defer Tabs and other elements until each has an authored typed contract; Tabs needs a
  coordinated tablist/tab/panel schema that its CSS record does not provide. Do not promise every
  CSS record or claim complete coverage. Utilities and declarations are not catalog components
  unless a real renderer exposes them as components.
- **Basic Catalog:** preserve its standard layout vocabulary and compose Pantoken-specific
  components with it where supported.
- **Basic Catalog:** preserve its standard layout vocabulary. A2UI v1.0 permits Pantoken components
  to use their own `@catalogId` alongside Basic Catalog components.
- **Docs:** add a searchable, browse-only catalog with schemas, support status, and raw JSON.
  Registration examples are web-only; native has no registration snippets. Defer live previews.

## Architecture and safety constraints

- The version gate found a mismatch between the current SDK overview and published renderer
  bundles. Target v1.0 only. Verify v1.0 catalog and Universal registration APIs against released
  React/Lit/Angular packages before claiming support.
- If those released SDKs do not support v1.0 Universal components, stop at the adapter gate and
  choose between waiting for compatible SDK releases and building framework-specific v1.0
  adapters. Do not fall back to v0.9.
- The schema spike must identify the canonical source for typed properties, child/slot rules,
  events/functions, icons, and accessibility behavior. Do not assume CSS modifier metadata supplies
  these contracts. If substantial new metadata or renderer behavior is required, revise the coverage
  and release scope before building the catalog.
- Before bridge implementation, define a strict component and property allowlist; reject unknown
  components and props, raw HTML/markup, unsafe URLs, unrecognized icon names, and arbitrary action
  or function execution. Map allowed actions only to explicit Pantoken behavior and safe events.
  Add negative tests for rejected inputs.
- Keep the runtime bridge browser-safe and Node-free. Do not import `@cssdoc/*`, catalog generators,
  or other build-only code into `renderers/web-components`; generation belongs in `ai/` build
  tooling.
- Give the catalog a stable, immutable, versioned `catalogId` (a `/vN/` identity, not a mutable
  `latest` URL). Treat component/prop removal, renames, required-prop changes, and incompatible
  semantics as breaking; additions that preserve old messages are additive. Tie regeneration and
  explicit version changes to the InstUI upgrade/deprecation workflow so upstream drift cannot
  silently alter the published contract.
- Update `ASSURANCE.md` and `SECURITY.md` if the catalog or bridge adds input surfaces or controls.

## Milestones

1. **Verification and schema/security spike.** Record the exact published package versions and the
   v1.0 Universal compatibility gap. Inspect Button, Tabs, and Tooltip; establish limited initial
   coverage and missing canonical metadata. Specify the allowlist and negative security cases.
2. **Catalog contract and generator.** Add the canonical A2UI 1.0 web catalog in `ai/` for Button
   and Tooltip, with explicit typed properties/actions/children, a stable versioned `catalogId`,
   and Basic Catalog composition via v1.0 semantics. Test schema validity, coverage, and drift.
   Publish the catalog and agent guidance with changesets for changed package output.
3. **Universal web bridge.** Implement the thin A2UI 1.0 Universal Web Component integration over
   existing Button and Tooltip elements only after the SDK gate passes. Reuse existing behavior;
   add no native UI kit and no duplicated rendering implementation. Test allowlisted props,
   children, actions, and rejected input.
4. **Docs catalog browser.** Generate static browser data from the same catalog source. Reuse the
   shadcn browser's search/static-data patterns, not its install commands or previews. Show
   per-client support, schemas, props, children, actions, raw JSON, and v1.0 web-only registration
   examples; localize new UI in English and Hungarian. Label Tabs and other unshipped components
   unsupported rather than implying full coverage.
5. **Agent evaluations, release, and drift gates.** Keep existing A2UI token-theming evaluations.
   Add positive web catalog routing and negative evaluations for invented components, invalid
   properties, and unsupported native registration. Update `use-a2ui` so agents use the Pantoken
   catalog for supported web clients and the Basic Catalog plus Pantoken tokens for native. Run
   focused tests, security checks, package checks, and publish checks. Ship each independently
   releasable package change with its changeset; follow repository release policy for docs-only
   work.

## Expected source areas

- `formats/components/src/` and `renderers/web-components/src/` — source-contract audit and web
  component behavior.
- `ai/pantoken-ai/catalogs/`, `ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/`, and package metadata — canonical catalog,
  generation, published assets, and version/drift checks.
- `renderers/web-components/` — thin Universal Web Component bridge, with no build-only imports.
- `docs/scripts/`, `docs/a2ui/`, and `docs/.vitepress/theme/` — generated static data, browser,
  routing, localization, and focused tests.
- `packages/scaffold/skills/use-a2ui/` and `packages/scaffold/assets/` — updated skill and shared
  consumer guidance.
- `ai/pantoken-ai/evals/` and renderer tests — positive and negative agent/bridge behavior.
- `ASSURANCE.md`, `SECURITY.md`, package documentation, and `.changeset/` — security and release
  updates when applicable.

## Verification

- Verify v1.0 Universal registration and catalog composition against the exact released SDKs before
  adding any React/Lit/Angular support claim. Do not validate by using 0.9.1 packages.
- Use the Button/Tabs/Tooltip spike to validate schema-source sufficiency; test only Button and
  Tooltip in the initial catalog, and mark Tabs/other components unsupported until their contracts
  are defined.
- Validate the generated catalog against the selected A2UI schema and assert its versioned ID,
  allowlist, and drift behavior.
- Test web registration and property/child/icon/event behavior, including unsafe/unknown inputs;
  verify the browser runtime graph remains Node-free.
- Verify the docs browser uses generated catalog data, localizes its UI, and labels native support
  as schema-only without native registration examples.
- Run existing and new A2UI Waza evaluations, focused package tests, `vp check`, and applicable
  publish checks. Add changesets for package output and public behavior changes.

   delays, and slotted trigger content, with text content rendered safely via `textContent`.

   must decide which components can be supported without inventing undocumented behavior.

 - **Protocol:** use A2UI 1.0 only, as directed. Do not downgrade to 0.9.
 - **Web-first v1:** target React, Lit, and Angular through one A2UI Universal Web Component bridge
   over `@pantoken/web-components` only after exact released SDK versions prove v1.0 support. The
   latest React/Angular packages checked do not yet establish that contract.

   this project. Mark them as schema-only/no Pantoken component renderer in the support matrix.
   Native apps continue using A2UI's Basic Catalog and Pantoken's existing native token outputs; do
   not advertise the Pantoken custom catalog as registered on those clients.

   `ai/`; the thin browser bridge lives with the existing web components. Do not make a blanket
   package that re-exports every renderer.

   schemas. Defer Tabs and other elements until each has an authored typed contract; Tabs needs a
   coordinated tablist/tab/panel schema that its CSS record does not provide. Do not promise every
   CSS record or claim complete coverage. Utilities and declarations are not catalog components
   unless a real renderer exposes them as components.

   components with it where supported.

   Registration examples are web-only; native has no registration snippets. Defer live previews.

   bundles. Target v1.0 only. Verify v1.0 catalog and Universal registration APIs against released
   React/Lit/Angular packages before claiming support.

   choose between waiting for compatible SDK releases and building framework-specific v1.0
   adapters. Do not fall back to v0.9.

   or function execution. Map allowed actions only to explicit Pantoken behavior and safe events.

---
name: use-a2ui
description: Inspect an app's installed A2UI renderer and apply pantoken tokens or icons through its supported theme API. Use for A2UI renderer theming or native token output, not transport-only or generic pantoken tasks.
---

# Use pantoken with A2UI

Use this skill when a consumer app combines pantoken with an A2UI renderer. Pantoken supplies
design tokens and icons; A2UI supplies the UI protocol and framework-specific renderers. For
token-only work, reuse the installed A2UI renderer rather than adding a runtime, transport, renderer,
or custom catalog.

## Do not use this skill for

Don't use this skill for A2UI protocol or transport questions that don't involve pantoken, or
generic pantoken styling without A2UI. Use it for custom catalogs only when the user explicitly
requests one.

## 1. Identify the client and versions

Inspect the app's package manifest, lockfile, and installed packages. Identify the actual A2UI
renderer, its protocol version, and how the host framework applies themes. Check the current
[official SDK table](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/) and
[client integration guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/) rather than assuming all
frameworks support the same protocol version or styling API. A2UI v1.0 delegates branding to the
renderer; don't put theme properties in v1.0 protocol messages.

## 2. Apply pantoken to the existing renderer

- **Web Basic Catalog:** Follow the current A2UI docs for its `--a2ui-*` custom properties. Read
  the installed renderer's stylesheet or version-matched docs to confirm each property. Use
  pantoken's `--instui-*` custom properties only after resolving a semantically matching,
  correctly typed token from `@pantoken/tokens`. Load `@pantoken/css` so those tokens are defined.
  Keep the mapping scoped when the app needs multiple themes; don't hard-code color values or
  invent A2UI or InstUI property names.
- **Native clients:** Use pantoken's existing target output for the host: `pantoken generate
  flutter`, `compose`, or `swift`, as appropriate. Follow the A2UI renderer's native theme API;
  CSS custom properties do not apply to native views.
- **Other web frameworks:** Choose the matching official A2UI renderer first, then use its supported
  theming mechanism. Don't assume React-specific setup applies to Lit or Angular.
- **Icons:** For surrounding web UI, use `@pantoken/web-components` or `@pantoken/icons`. For icons
  inside an A2UI surface, verify the selected catalog's icon API; only add a custom component when
  the user asks for one.

## 3. Extend only when requested

If the user asks for a custom A2UI catalog, follow A2UI's
[catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/) and the host renderer's registration
API. A catalog defines agent-facing components and functions; pantoken tokens don't implement those
components or behaviors. Preserve the renderer's accessibility, focus, and interaction contracts.
Handle protocol transports only when explicitly in scope.

## 4. Verify

Run the host app's relevant type checks and tests. Verify the theme in each supported color scheme,
including contrast and keyboard/focus behavior. Confirm every `--instui-*` reference exists in the
installed token package and every `--a2ui-*` property matches the installed A2UI renderer version.

## References

- [A2UI v1.0 protocol](https://a2ui.org/specification/v1.0-a2ui/)
- [A2UI SDKs](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/)
- [A2UI client integration](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/)
- [A2UI catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/)

<overview>
The user wants Pantoken to publish an A2UI catalog that gives agents a constrained vocabulary of Pantoken-style components, with a browsable docs catalog and reusable web rendering. The user explicitly requires A2UI 1.0, web-first scope, and no new native UI kits; implementation is gated by verifying actual SDK support and schema coverage.
</overview>

<history>
1. The user initially requested first-class A2UI support, specifying the work belongs in `ai/`, not `renderers/`, and asked for an incremental implementation with conventional commits and changesets on the `a2ui` branch.
   - Earlier commits already added the A2UI skill and shared agent guidance: `a942d5f64` and `7e135d529`.
   - No catalog implementation had begun.

2. The user refined the goal to constrain agents to Pantoken-style components and reuse Pantoken’s existing rendering, property mapping, icon handling, and behavior.
   - The plan was updated to include a shared web bridge and searchable docs catalog.

3. The user supplied a detailed review identifying blockers:
   - Flutter, Swift, and Compose emit token constants, not UI components, so native adapters would require new UI kits.
   - Require verification of SDK versions, protocol support, Universal Web Component compatibility, and Basic Catalog composition.
   - Spike Button, Tabs, and Tooltip because CSS records do not establish A2UI props, children, and events.
   - Put security constraints and negative tests before bridge implementation.
   - Define catalog versioning and drift controls; add negative agent evals; update the skill.
   - Split into independently shippable milestones.

4. The user confirmed web-first scope and most recently explicitly directed: **“we should be using a2ui 1.0 not 0.9.”**
   - Accordingly, the plan now targets A2UI 1.0 only; no fallback to 0.9.
   - Since the latest published React and Angular bundles did not demonstrate v1.0 Universal support, the chosen pragmatic route is to implement the v1.0 catalog/component contract and verify it through Lit, while marking React/Angular runtime support pending. Do not build Pantoken-specific React/Angular renderers without a separate decision.
</history>

<work_done>
**Plan and tracking**
- Updated the session plan at [plan.md](/Users/dwahl/.copilot/session-state/39e9b1ff-f8f1-4f49-bb37-3badfe65e332/plan.md) to reflect:
  - A2UI 1.0 only.
  - Web-first, with Lit as the initial verified runtime target and React/Angular pending SDK proof.
  - Native clients are schema-only/no Pantoken component renderer; they use Basic Catalog plus Pantoken token output.
  - Initial catalog coverage is Button and Tooltip; Tabs and other elements are deferred until typed contracts are authored.
  - Basic Catalog components should be reused by reference with v1.0 `@catalogId` semantics.
- Updated session SQL todos. SDK verification, schema spike, and initial coverage inventory were marked done. The catalog-contract todo remains marked blocked from the previous SDK-route question and needs status/description updated to match the user’s v1.0 direction and chosen Lit-first route.
- The repository was clean on branch `a2ui` at the last status check. No repository source files, manifests, changesets, or commits have been created during this turn.

**Research completed**
- Verified official Universal Component guidance: Zod `ComponentApi`, `A2uiLitElement`, `WebComponentImplementation`, and v1.0 Basic Catalog composition.
- Checked latest npm package metadata: `@a2ui/web_core` 0.15.0, `@a2ui/react` 0.15.0, `@a2ui/lit` 0.15.0, and `@a2ui/angular` 0.14.0.
- Inspected published bundles: React and Angular use the `@a2ui/web_core/v0_9/universal` path; the current evidence does not establish a shared v1.0 Universal path for those packages. Lit exposes the Universal API and v1.0 Basic Catalog path.
- Confirmed CSS component records lack typed A2UI schemas. Button’s web-element contract is in JSDoc; Tabs needs a coordinated tablist/tab/panel contract; Tooltip has `tip`, `placement`, delay attributes, and slotted trigger content, with tooltip text written through `textContent`.
</work_done>

<technical_details>
- The SDK overview and published renderer bundles appear inconsistent: official documentation describes v1.0 support, while the latest React and Angular bundles inspected reference v0.9 Universal code. Do not claim React/Angular v1.0 runtime compatibility without further verification.
- A2UI v1.0 supports component-level `@catalogId`, allowing Pantoken components to coexist with Basic Catalog components. The docs demonstrate reusing Basic Catalog component implementations by reference; avoid copying Basic schemas.

Button, Tabs, and Tooltip implementations are in their respective files under [renderers/web-components/src/elements/](/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/renderers/web-components/src/elements).

- The browser runtime in `renderers/web-components` must stay Node-free. Catalog generation belongs in `ai/` build tooling.

import { buttonCss } from "@pantoken/components";
import type { ElementDefinition } from "../lib/context.ts";

/**
 * `<instui-button>` — a token-styled `<button>`. The `variant` attribute maps to the `-color-<variant>`
 * modifier (`secondary`, `tertiary`, `success`, `danger`, `ai`, …); `margin` adds spacing around the
 * host (InstUI keywords like `small` / `medium large`); slotted content is the label.
 *
 * It is also a native invoker: `popovertarget` (with optional `popovertargetaction`) toggles any
 * light-DOM `[popover]` such as `<instui-context-view>`, `<instui-popover>`, or `<instui-tray>`, and
 * `command`/`commandfor` drives the command-based components (`<instui-modal>` with `--show`/`--close`,
 * etc.). The id is forwarded to the inner button via the invoker IDL, so it resolves across the shadow
 * boundary and may point forward to an element declared later in the document.
 *
 * @example
 * ```html
 * <instui-button variant="primary" margin="small">Save changes</instui-button>
 * <instui-button variant="danger" margin="small">Delete</instui-button>
 * <instui-button popovertarget="cv">Details</instui-button>
 * <instui-context-view id="cv">More about this item.</instui-context-view>
 * ```
 */
export const button: ElementDefinition = {
  name: "button",
  define: (ctx) =>
    ctx.wrapper(
      "instui-button",
      buttonCss(ctx.I),
      (host) =>
        `<button class="${ctx.variantClass("button", host)}" part="button"><slot></slot></button>`,
      { invoker: true },
    ),
};
