 - `<instui-modal open>` — renders a real `<dialog>`; the `open` attribute drives `showModal()`/`close()`,
   and native dismissal (`Esc`/backdrop) reflects back and fires a `close` event.
 - `<instui-context-view>`, `<instui-popover>`, `<instui-tray placement="start|end|top|bottom" size="…">`
   — native popovers; toggle from a button with `popovertarget`/`command`.
 - `<instui-in-place-edit value="…" readonly>` — click-to-edit field; commits on Enter/blur (fires a
   `change` event), reverts on Escape.
 
 The module is Node-safe: element classes are defined inside `register()`, which no-ops when there is
 no DOM. Call `register(customElements)` manually if you need to control timing.
 
 ## API
 
 - **`register(registry?, options?): void`** — define the custom elements into a registry (defaults to `globalThis.customElements`). No-op when there is no DOM, so it's safe to import during SSR or a build. `options.prefix` sets the tag prefix, mirroring the CSS layer: pass a non-empty string like `x` for `<x-icon>`. A prefix is always applied (a custom-element name must contain a hyphen), so an omitted, empty, or nullish prefix falls back to the default `instui` (`<instui-icon>`). `options.locale` (BCP47 tag), `options.strings` (partial override), and `options.dir` (`"ltr" | "rtl"`) localize the behavioral elements.
 - **`iconSvg(name, resolve?): string`** — resolve an icon name to inline SVG (empty string when unknown). Pure; the element renders the result.
 - **`ELEMENTS`** — the tuple of base (unprefixed) element names this package registers (e.g. `icon`, `date-input`).
 - **`DEFAULT_PREFIX`** — the default tag prefix, `"instui"`.
 - **`WebComponentStrings`**, **`ENGLISH_STRINGS`**, **`makeStrings`**, **`resolveFirstDay`** — the locale string contract, plus the full 44-locale bundle set and `registerLocalized` helper.
 
 ## Related
 
 - Styles the elements with `@pantoken/components` and reads glyphs from `@pantoken/icons`.
 - Pairs with `@pantoken/css` for the base `--instui-*` custom properties.
 - Locale bundles and `registerLocalized` are exported from this package; translations are generated from `src/i18n.json` and the repository `/l10n` PO catalogs.
 - Wrapped by the per-framework helpers: `@pantoken/angular`, `@pantoken/react`, `@pantoken/svelte`, and `@pantoken/vue`.

- React: `@pantoken/react` (`<Icon>`, `useToken`, `TokenProvider`). For InstUI's full React components use `@instructure/ui-*`.
- Vue: `@pantoken/vue` (plugin). Svelte: `@pantoken/svelte` (`icon` action). Angular: `@pantoken/angular`.
- React Native: `@pantoken/react-native` (StyleSheet-friendly objects, no CSS vars).
- Markdown: `@pantoken/react-markdown` (react-markdown → InstUI), `@pantoken/rehype` (`:icon:` tokens).

## A2UI clients

When combining pantoken with A2UI, distinguish token theming from the A2UI protocol, transport,
renderer, and catalog. Claude Code has a dedicated `use-a2ui` skill; other agents can follow these
rules:

- Inspect the installed A2UI renderer and protocol version, and check the current official SDK docs.
  Do not assume framework clients support the same versions or styling APIs.
- For the web Basic Catalog, use its documented `--a2ui-*` properties and map only to semantically
  matching `--instui-*` tokens verified in `@pantoken/tokens`. Load `@pantoken/css`; don't invent
  property names or hard-code colors.
- For native clients, use the existing pantoken output for that host (`flutter`, `compose`, or
  `swift`) and the renderer's native theme API; CSS custom properties do not apply to native views.
- A2UI v1.0 delegates branding to the renderer. Do not put theme properties in v1.0 protocol
  messages or add a runtime/renderer/catalog for token-only work.

# pantoken (Instructure design tokens & icons)

When styling this project, use pantoken components, icons and tokens.

- First distinguish a maintained application from a standalone artifact. For a single HTML mockup
  or sendable email, follow the `create-pantoken-mockup` skill instead of scaffolding a project.
- In a shadcn project, discover CSS items with `shadcn search @pantoken`, inspect with `shadcn view
  @pantoken/<item>`, and install with `shadcn add @pantoken/<item>`. These are styles and metadata,
  not React components. `@pantoken/shadcn` is only the CSS-variable bridge.

- Tokens are CSS custom properties `--instui-<group>-<name>` (e.g. `--instui-color-background-brand`).
  Use `var(--instui-*)` references, never hard-coded colours, so theming keeps working. Resolve real
  names from `@pantoken/tokens` — don't guess. If the exact token name is unknown, state that the
  token name must be verified against `@pantoken/tokens` and provide a placeholder like
  `--instui-<group>-<name>` with a comment noting it needs confirmation.
- Web app: `import "@pantoken/css/inject";` to define the properties.
- A2UI: use the installed framework renderer. For its web Basic Catalog, verify the current
  `--a2ui-*` properties and map only to matching `--instui-*` tokens from `@pantoken/tokens`;
  native clients use pantoken's existing platform outputs. Check renderer/protocol versions first.
- User preferences are automatic, not opt-in variants: `prefers-reduced-motion`, `prefers-contrast`,
  `prefers-reduced-transparency`, and forced colors. Preserve static loading feedback and disabled
  cues. More contrast strengthens boundaries; less removes decorative shadows without reducing text
  contrast. Ready token sheets follow the system scheme; explicit `data-pantoken-scheme` light/dark
  pins win. Use `properties.css` plus `scope.css` for nested themes, not multiple root theme sheets.
- Icons: `@pantoken/web-components` (`<instui-icon name="…">`) or `@pantoken/react` (`<Icon>`).

## Build tools

- `@pantoken/vite` · `@pantoken/next` · `@pantoken/webpack` · `@pantoken/tailwind` · `@pantoken/postcss`

## Theming other systems

- `@pantoken/shadcn` · `@pantoken/bootstrap` · `@pantoken/storybook`

  verified `--instui-*` tokens; use existing pantoken native outputs for native clients.

## Native & other ecosystems (CLI: `pantoken generate <target>`)

- swift, android, compose, flutter, rust, wordpress, vanilla, drupal, jekyll, hugo — add
	`--icons`, `--theme`, `--out`, and for rust `--format`.
- Check https://pantoken.app/target-compatibility.json before claiming a supported host version;
	its `$schema` field identifies the published schema. Verified releases and environments are
	bounded evidence, not promises about newer versions.

## AI tooling for consumers

- `@pantoken/ai` provides installable agent assets: `AGENTS.md`, `llms.txt`, and editor/assistant
	rules for Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, and Claude Code.
- The Claude Code assets include `use-a2ui` for A2UI integrations; shared agent rules also cover
	version-aware token theming.
- CLI: `npx pantoken-ai init [--tool <all|agents|llms|cursor|copilot|windsurf|claude>] [--dir <path>]`.

## Design & interchange

- `@pantoken/dtcg` (W3C DTCG JSON) · `@pantoken/scss` · `@pantoken/figma` (Figma Variables) · `@pantoken/email`

---
name: use-a2ui
description: Use Pantoken's constrained A2UI 1.0 component catalog or theme an installed A2UI renderer with Pantoken tokens. Use for A2UI work involving Pantoken, not transport-only or generic Pantoken tasks.
---

# Use Pantoken with A2UI

Use this skill when a consumer app combines Pantoken with A2UI. A2UI supplies the protocol and
framework-specific renderers; Pantoken supplies tokens, icons, and a small set of styled components.
Use A2UI 1.0 only. Do not fall back to A2UI 0.9.

## Do not use this skill for

Don't use this skill for A2UI protocol or transport questions that don't involve Pantoken, or for
generic Pantoken styling without A2UI.

## 1. Identify the client and versions

Inspect the app's package manifest, lockfile, and installed packages. Confirm the A2UI protocol
version and the client framework's supported SDK version from the
[official SDK table](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/) and
[client integration guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/). A2UI 1.0 delegates branding
to the renderer; don't put theme properties in protocol messages.

## 2. Prefer the Pantoken catalog for verified Lit clients

For A2UI 1.0 Lit clients, use the published Pantoken catalog and Universal components:

- Install `@pantoken/ai` and `@pantoken/web-components`.
- Register `pantokenA2uiCatalog` with `registerPantokenA2uiComponents()` from
  `@pantoken/web-components/a2ui`, alongside A2UI's Basic Catalog.
- Reference Pantoken components with the catalog's `@catalogId`.
- Use only the components and properties listed in the catalog JSON at
  `@pantoken/ai/a2ui/catalog-v1.json` or the
  [Pantoken A2UI Catalog](https://pantoken.app/a2ui/). The v1 catalog currently contains
  `PantokenButton` and `PantokenTooltip`; don't invent additional Pantoken components or properties.
- The catalog defines no executable functions. Its actions dispatch through A2UI's normal
  action-handling path; the host application remains responsible for authorization.

React and Angular v1.0 runtime support has not been verified. For those clients, use A2UI's Basic
Catalog and the installed renderer's theme API instead of claiming the Pantoken Universal components
are supported. Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose have schema-only support; Pantoken does not
provide native component renderers.

## 3. Theme the Basic Catalog and other verified renderers

- **Web Basic Catalog:** Follow the current A2UI docs for its `--a2ui-*` custom properties. Read the
  installed renderer's stylesheet or version-matched docs to confirm each property. Use Pantoken's
  `--instui-*` custom properties only after resolving a semantically matching, correctly typed token
  from `@pantoken/tokens`. Load `@pantoken/css` so those tokens are defined. Keep mappings scoped
  when the app needs multiple themes; don't hard-code colors or invent property names.
- **Native clients:** Use Pantoken's existing target output for the host:
  `pantoken generate flutter`, `compose`, or `swift`, as appropriate. Follow the A2UI renderer's
  native theme API; CSS custom properties don't apply to native views.
- **Icons:** For surrounding web UI, use `@pantoken/web-components` or `@pantoken/icons`. For icons
  inside an A2UI surface, verify the selected catalog's icon API; don't invent icon props.

## 4. Extend only when requested

If the user explicitly requests a different custom catalog, follow A2UI's
[catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/) and the host renderer's registration
API. Preserve strict property allowlists, avoid raw HTML and URL-bearing props, and don't add
executable catalog functions without an explicit design and security review. A catalog schema is
not an authorization boundary; the host must authorize action effects.

## 5. Verify

Run the host app's relevant type checks and tests. Verify the theme in each supported color scheme,
including contrast, keyboard behavior, and focus visibility. Confirm every `--instui-*` reference
exists in the installed token package and every `--a2ui-*` property matches the installed A2UI
renderer version.

## References

- [A2UI v1.0 protocol](https://a2ui.org/specification/v1.0-a2ui/)
- [A2UI SDKs](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/)
- [A2UI client integration](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-integration/)
- [A2UI catalog guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/defining-a-catalog/)

- **`iconSvg(name, resolve?): string`** — resolve an icon name to inline SVG (empty string when unknown). Pure; the element renders the result.
- **`ELEMENTS`** — the tuple of base (unprefixed) element names this package registers (e.g. `icon`, `date-input`).
- **`DEFAULT_PREFIX`** — the default tag prefix, `"instui"`.
- **`WebComponentStrings`**, **`ENGLISH_STRINGS`**, **`makeStrings`**, **`resolveFirstDay`** — the locale string contract, plus the full 44-locale bundle set and `registerLocalized` helper.

## A2UI 1.0

For verified Lit clients, the optional `./a2ui` entry registers Pantoken's Universal components and
catalog alongside A2UI's Basic Catalog:

```ts
import { basicCatalog } from "@a2ui/web_core/catalogs/basic/v1";
import { MessageProcessor } from "@a2ui/web_core";
import { pantokenA2uiCatalog, registerPantokenA2uiComponents } from "@pantoken/web-components/a2ui";

registerPantokenA2uiComponents();
const processor = new MessageProcessor([basicCatalog, pantokenA2uiCatalog]);
```

Install `@a2ui/web_core` and `lit` in the host app. The catalog currently contains only
`PantokenButton` and `PantokenTooltip`. See the [published catalog and support status](https://pantoken.app/a2ui/);
React and Angular v1.0 runtime support is pending verification, and native platforms have schema-only
support.

## Related

- Styles the elements with `@pantoken/components` and reads glyphs from `@pantoken/icons`.
- Pairs with `@pantoken/css` for the base `--instui-*` custom properties.
- Locale bundles and `registerLocalized` are exported from this package; translations are generated from `src/i18n.json` and the repository `/l10n` PO catalogs.
- Wrapped by the per-framework helpers: `@pantoken/angular`, `@pantoken/react`, `@pantoken/svelte`, and `@pantoken/vue`.

## License

MIT

data.summaryContent:
<overview>
The user wants Pantoken A2UI support centered on a published, constrained catalog in `ai/`, with a Lit web-component adapter that reuses Pantoken’s existing styling and behavior. The agreed scope is A2UI 1.0, a browsable docs catalog, and schema-only native support—no native UI kits; React and Angular runtime support remains unverified. The user requested incremental conventional commits and changesets on the `a2ui` branch, and explicitly said **not to run translations** because they will handle them later.
</overview>

<history>
1. The user requested first-class A2UI support and clarified that the catalog belongs in `ai/`, not `renderers/`.
   - The scope evolved to a constrained Pantoken component vocabulary that uses existing renderers and behavior.
   - The user chose A2UI 1.0, Lit-first verification, a browsable docs catalog, and schema-only native support.
   - They asked for incremental conventional commits and changesets on `a2ui`.

2. The implementation added a canonical catalog for `PantokenButton` and `PantokenTooltip`, an allowlist validator/generator, Lit Universal components, security guidance, agent skills, and a docs catalog browser.
   - Button and tooltip text are rendered as text; undeclared properties and unsupported variants/placements are rejected.
   - Actions flow through A2UI’s handler; host applications remain responsible for authorization.
   - Native renderers are not being built.

3. The user’s latest instruction was: “don't run translations, I'll do that myself later.”
   - No translation command was run after this instruction.
   - `docs:check:drift` was run earlier and reported 840 missing translation units across 42 locales. This remains deferred per the user.

4. During validation, the docs build’s normal asset pipeline launched a large automated accessibility audit unrelated to the new catalog and ran for many minutes. It was stopped; a subsequent attempt also launched the audit despite setting the skip variable and was stopped.
   - A targeted English docs build then succeeded by directly skipping the accessibility-refresh script, generating English API/CSS docs, and building VitePress. The generated `/a2ui/` HTML and `/a2ui/catalog.json` were checked.

5. A package export issue remains:
   - `@pantoken/ai/a2ui/catalog-v1.json` was added to `ai/pantoken-ai/package.json` and Node import resolution succeeded once.
   - After running `vp pack`, that export disappeared. `ai/pantoken-ai/vite.config.ts` has `exports: true`, which regenerates the export map. The next step is to preserve the hand-managed export map, likely by setting `exports: false`, then rebuild and retest.

6. The docs API build modified `l10n/docs.api.pot` with a large generated diff, mostly apparent source-catalog reordering/duplicate reference changes. Inspect before committing; do not blindly include unrelated generated noise.

</history>

<work_done>
Files created:
- `ai/pantoken-ai/catalogs/pantoken-v1.json`: A2UI 1.0 schema with only Button and Tooltip.
- `ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/generate-a2ui-catalog.ts`: validates strict contracts and generates renderer/docs copies.

- `ai/pantoken-ai/evals/use-a2ui/tasks/unsupported-component.yaml`: negative eval task.

- `.changeset/lovely-knives-throw.md` and `.changeset/neat-pants-lick.md`.

- Scaffold A2UI skill and shared agent guidance (`AGENTS.md`, Copilot, Windsurf, and `llms.txt` assets).

Validation:

- AI package: 32 tests passed; build and `publint` passed.

- Targeted A2UI lint/type checks and catalog generator `--check` passed.

<technical_details>
- The SDK package is `@a2ui/web_core` 0.15.0 and supports A2UI protocol 1.0. Do not add a 0.9 fallback.
- The catalog ID is `https://pantoken.app/a2ui/catalog/v1/catalog.json`; intended npm subpath is `@pantoken/ai/a2ui/catalog-v1.json`.
- Runtime imports A2UI/Lit as optional peers; `@pantoken/web-components/a2ui` is opt-in so the package’s default entry does not require the A2UI peer.
- `A2uiLitElement` renders into Shadow DOM. Tooltip initialization must query `this.renderRoot`, not the host’s light DOM; teardown uses the shared `initTooltip` cleanup.
- `KeyboardEvent` test dispatch must set `composed: true` to simulate a real keydown crossing the shadow boundary to the document listener.
- The web renderer safely interpolates labels/tips as Lit text and does not expose raw HTML or URL props. A2UI actions are not an authorization boundary.
- `vp pack` rewrites package exports when `exports: true` is set in `ai/pantoken-ai/vite.config.ts`; hand-managed exports must be preserved there.
- Package assets are sourced from `packages/scaffold/assets`; `vp run test` regenerates them, then `vp pack` builds the package. AI generation copies the A2UI skill from `packages/scaffold/skills/use-a2ui/SKILL.md`.
- The docs asset pipeline includes a large accessibility audit; the targeted docs build succeeded without that audit. The regular docs build was interrupted and should not be claimed as passing.
- Do not run any translation tasks; the user will handle translations.

</technical_details>

- `renderers/web-components/tests/a2ui.test.ts` — integration and unsafe-text coverage; full suite passed.
- `packages/scaffold/assets/AGENTS.md`, `copilot-instructions.md`, `windsurf.md`, `llms.txt` — shared agent guidance now points to the catalog and support boundaries.
- `packages/scaffold/skills/use-a2ui/SKILL.md` — canonical skill; the AI package’s copy is generated from it.

- `ASSURANCE.md` and `SECURITY.md` — document the added input surface and controls.

- `.changeset/lovely-knives-throw.md` and `.changeset/neat-pants-lick.md` — AI/scaffold and web-components release bumps.
</important_files>

<next_steps>
1. Set `exports: false` in `ai/pantoken-ai/vite.config.ts` so `vp pack` preserves the manual `./a2ui/catalog-v1.json` export. Rebuild, run `publint`, and verify Node can import the JSON subpath after packing.
2. Inspect `l10n/docs.api.pot`; retain only directly relevant API catalog changes, or leave out unrelated generated churn. Do not run translations.
3. Re-run `git diff --check`, inspect status, and confirm generated files are not staged accidentally.
4. Create the requested incremental conventional commits with the required Copilot co-author trailer. Include both changesets with the core catalog/renderer commit; commit the docs browser separately. Do not stage unrelated files.
5. In the final status, note that locale translation remains intentionally deferred and `docs:check:drift` is expected to remain failing until the user translates the new strings.
</next_steps>
